text:
**I’d pick Starling Bank’s debit Mastercard for everyday spending abroad.** Its UK personal current account has no monthly fee, and when you pay in local currency, Starling uses the Mastercard exchange rate without adding a foreign transaction fee or exchange-rate markup. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/travel/?utm_source=openai))

It’s also a good choice for cash: you can withdraw the equivalent of **£300 per day** abroad without a Starling fee. The ATM operator can still charge its own fee, so check the screen before confirming. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/travel/?utm_source=openai))

**If you already have a Chase UK debit card, I’d use that rather than open another account just for the trip.** For card purchases, you get the same Mastercard exchange rate with no fee from Chase. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/support/travel-with-chase/?af_ad=boosted&af_channel=organic-social&c=mkt-686_uk_gl_dgt_oso_fbig_eng_xdv_pr_adp_at11_reach_awareness&pid=facebook-instagram&utm_source=openai))

**Whichever card you use, choose the local currency, not pounds.** For example, if a terminal in Spain offers EUR or GBP, choose EUR. That lets your card handle the conversion rather than accepting the retailer’s usually less favourable rate. ([help.starlingbank.com](https://help.starlingbank.com/joint/topics/travelling-overseas/what-do-the-different-debit-card-exchange-rates-mean/?utm_source=openai))
